record.paper_title: Aspects of Nonabelian Group Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can one prove that a chosen group platform is secure for non-commutative cryptographic constructions such as public-key exchange protocols, digital-signature schemes, and authentication schemes?

evidence.quote: 3. How can we show a group is provably secure for the new non-commutative schemes such as public key exchanges, digital signatures and authentication?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a non-abelian (in general, infinite or finite) group, called a platform group, on which one builds non-commutative cryptographic constructions such as a public-key exchange protocol, a digital signature scheme, or an authentication scheme. The security of such constructions typically relies on the conjectured computational hardness of certain group-theoretic problems in G (for example, the conjugacy search problem, the word problem, the simultaneous conjugacy problem, the decomposition problem, or related problems).

Develop a general framework, together with explicit criteria on the platform group G, that allows one to prove (in a rigorous reductionist sense, e.g. by reducing the security of the protocol against a specified adversarial model to a precisely formulated, average-case hard computational problem in G) that the chosen platform G yields provably secure non-commutative public-key exchange protocols, digital signature schemes, and authentication schemes.

Concretely: identify a class of platform groups G and an associated family of group-theoretic problems P(G) such that
(i) P(G) is hard in the average case under a natural distribution on instances,
(ii) the security of the proposed key exchange / signature / authentication scheme based on G can be reduced to P(G) in a standard cryptographic security model (e.g. IND-CPA, EUF-CMA, or analogous notions), and
(iii) the reduction yields concrete, quantifiable security parameters.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of providing fully reductionist provable security for non-commutative group-based cryptographic schemes (key exchange, signatures, authentication) over a chosen platform group remains an active research problem. Recent works (e.g., the 2018 "Provably Secure Integration Cryptosystem on Non-Commutative Group", the generalization of LWE/LPN to "learning homomorphisms with noise" on non-abelian groups, and survey/status papers on polycyclic and quantum-era group-based cryptography from 2016–2022) propose partial frameworks and specific platform candidates but do not deliver a general solution. No comprehensive provable-security framework comparable to that available in the abelian/lattice setting has been established.

status_evidence.title: Provably Secure Integration Cryptosystem on Non-Commutative Group
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a specific cryptosystem on a non-commutative group with a security reduction, but limited to a particular construction.
status_evidence.claim: Partial provable-security results exist for specific non-commutative constructions, not a general framework.

status_evidence.title: Group-based Cryptography in the Quantum Era
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of group-based cryptography highlighting that average-case hardness for non-abelian platforms remains a key open issue.
status_evidence.claim: General provable security on non-commutative platforms is still open.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Learning Problems and Applications to Non-commutative Cryptography
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces learning homomorphisms with noise as an attempt to provide hard average-case problems on non-abelian groups.
status_evidence.claim: Frameworks exist for some hard problems but provable security of full schemes is partial.

status_evidence.title: The Status of Polycyclic Group-Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing provable security over chosen platform groups as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in surveys after 2011.
